title: He could quote the law.
paragraphs:
He could quote the law.
He just could not survive his own sermon.
Romans 2:21 is a blade: “You then, who teach others, do you not teach yourself?”
That is the terror of religion without surrender.

A man can stand in front of crowds.
Open the Bible.
Raise his voice.
Warn sinners.
Expose darkness.
And still go home unsaved.
Because preaching truth is not the same as bowing to Truth.

That is Paul’s wound in Romans 2. He is speaking to the man who knows the commandments, honors the standards, corrects the broken, and feels strong because he can spot sin in others. But beneath the polished words is a soul still untouched by repentance. Mouth full of doctrine. Heart full of distance.
And that is where this gets dangerous.

You can rebuke lust and still be ruled by secret craving.
You can denounce theft and still rob God of worship.
You can preach holiness and still hide rot under the robe.

Public fire.
Private ashes.

But here’s what we miss: Romans 2 is not just exposing hypocrites. It is exposing every one of us who ever tried to look righteous instead of being made righteous by Christ. The issue is not only that the man failed to practice what he preached. The deeper tragedy is that he trusted his position, his knowledge, his image, and his performance more than the mercy of God.
And no sermon can save a man who will not come to Jesus broken.
Only Christ can do that.

Jesus did not die for people who looked clean.
He died for people who finally admitted they were not.

This is the Gospel: the preacher, the teacher, the church kid, the moral man, the respectable woman, the person who knows every verse but still feels hollow inside — you can be washed. Not by your title. Not by your religious vocabulary. Not by your reputation. By the blood of Jesus alone.

So before you teach another lesson, ask the hard question:
Has the Word pierced me first?

Before you call others to repent, kneel.
Before you correct the crowd, let God correct you.
Before you preach Christ, make sure you are clinging to Christ.
Because the most dangerous place in the world is near the truth without being transformed by it.
And the most beautiful miracle is this: even the man who failed in the pulpit can still find mercy at the cross.

Repent.
Come clean.
Come low.
Come now.
Jesus is still saving the people religion could not fix.
“You then, who teach others, do you not teach yourself?” — Romans 2:21
